t: The Secretary of Defense may establish or develop installations and facilities under this title without regard to section 3648 of the Revised Statutes, as amended (31 U.S.C. 529), and sections 4774 and 9774 of title 10, United States Code. The authority to place permanent or temporary improvements on lands includes authority for surveys, administration, overhead, planning, and supervision incident to construction. That authority may be exercised before title to the land is approved under section 355 of the Revised Statutes, as amended (40 U.S.C. 255), and even though the land is held temporarily. The authority to acquire real estate or land includes authority to make surveys and to acquire land and interests in land (including temporary use), by gift, purchase, exchange of Government-owned land, or otherwise.

fable.w: This section only grants the Secretary of Defense authority to build installations and acquire land, waiving certain statutory restrictions. The tempting reading is that acquiring land by "gift, purchase, exchange" involves outside parties, but those are property transactions, not consultation, comment, hearings, advisory bodies, or a right to sue over a federal decision. No outside party is brought into any federal decisionmaking process.
fable.s: The Secretary of Defense may establish or develop installations and facilities under this title without regard to section 3648 of the Revised Statutes

opus.w: The section gives the Secretary of Defense authority to build installations and acquire land, and waives certain statutory requirements. Buying, exchanging or accepting land as a gift involves outside parties only as parties to a transaction, the same way a contract does. They are not consulted on a federal decision. No hearing, comment period, advisory body, consultation with states, rulemaking or right to sue is created.
opus.s: The authority to acquire real estate or land includes authority to make surveys and to acquire land and interests in land (including temporary use), by gift, purchase, exchange of Government-owned land, or otherwise.
opus.b:
1. **Reasoning.** The tempting reading is that acquiring land "by gift, purchase, exchange" involves outside parties such as landowners or donors, so it might count as participation. That fails the definition. A land deal is a property transaction, much like a contract. It does not involve consulting or coordinating with outsiders before a federal decision. The section only gives the Secretary construction and acquisition powers and waives certain legal requirements. It calls for no hearing, comment period, advisory body, consultation with outsiders, rulemaking or right to sue.

2. **Label.**

qwen_chat.w: This section grants the Secretary of Defense authority to establish facilities and acquire land. It describes internal administrative powers and does not require or recommend consultation with any parties outside the federal government. All actors mentioned (Secretary of Defense, Government-owned land) are inside the federal government.
qwen_chat.s: The Secretary of Defense may establish or develop installations and facilities under this title without regard to section 3648 of the Revised Statutes, as amended (31 U.S.C. 529), and sections 4774 and 9774 of title 10, United States Code.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "surveys" or "planning" imply some form of consultation with outside parties, but the text strictly limits the actors to the Secretary of Defense and federal authorities. There is no mention of public comment, advisory boards with non-federal members, or consultation with states or tribes. The text describes internal administrative powers and authorities for acquiring land and constructing facilities.
